newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes lower on poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes lower on poor demand.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed lower on poor demand, dampened by falls in Tokyo.

"There was little scattered interest. Nobody wants to trade actively ahead of May Day holiday tomorrow," a dealer said. Buyers also stayed at the sidelines on expectations of lower levels following the inflow of supply.

"Supply is seen coming back to the market. The wintering period is almost over," the dealer said. Producers are also offering lower levels for fear of more stocks in the market because of improved weather conditions. Only some hand-to-mouth business was seen.
Trading houses offered SMR CV at 332 cents, SMR L at 310 cents, SMR 5 at 269, SMR 10 at 256 and drum latex at 228 cents.
At the close, May RSS Ones buyer eased two cents to 275.50 cents ($1.09) a kg and May SMR 20 buyer was down a cent at 260.50 cents.
The INRO five-day moving average was Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg was 209.09 on April 29 against 209.86 on April 28.
The daily indicator price was 208.21 against 208.61.
